title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridors 2, 3, And 5 (Obigarm-Nurobod) Road Project

description.narrative: The Obigarm-Nurobod road section of the existing M41 highway, which carries about 3,000 vehicles per day, will be inundated once the HPP reservoir has filled to operating levels. The realignment of this road section through the river valley is not part of the Rogun HPP project. A bypass road must be completed and opened to traffic by latest November 2023, the date by which the rising water in the HPP reservoir will have inundated several critical sections of the M41 highway. No other part of Tajikistan's national highway network can provide for this traffic, and the only alternative route would represent a deviation of about 500 km. The government has requested ADB's assistance to construct a 72 km long road section that will bypass the HPP reservoir through mountainous terrain (the project road). It will be constructed to two-lane asphalt surfaced standard, and will include three tunnels with a total length of about 6 km, one high level bridge about 700 m long, and 13 shorter bridges with a total length of about 975 m. The construction of some parts of the project road started in 1988 (mostly earthworks) but was suspended following the abandonment of the Rogun HPP project.

Output: Design of the new road project improved Indicator: Enhance climate change resilience aspects of the detailed engineering design for Dangara-Guliston road Progress/Status: On 3 November 2023, the MOF sought ADB's approval to use savings from the G0683-TAJ project to update the Climate Resilience Assessment (CRA) due to anticipated substantive changes in the detailed design of the 49 km Dangara-Guliston road. These changes aimed to align the proposed Green Corridor Demonstration Project (GCDP) with the objectives of the Paris Agreement. On 9 February 2024, ADB approved the minor change in project scope, and on 19 February 2024, the MOT signed a $500,000 direct contract with Kocks Consult GmbH (Germany), in association with Finnish Overseas Consultants Ltd. (Finland) and SUE Design Institute for Transport Infrastructure (Tajikistan), to update the design of the road. On 13 September 2024, ADB approved variation order No.1 for the above CS-03 Contract, which included reallocation of person-months, adjustments to expenses and a 3.5-month contract extension from 18 July to 31 October 2024. The contract amount of $500,000 remained unchanged. The consultancy service is already completed. Data Source: Project final report by PMC Baseline year: 2024 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2024 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y
